fields.Major Events: Five cadets woke aboard the Moonraider in the middle of a losing battle, fighting astral reavers under a dying Captain Sardax until the scene froze and revealed itself as a simulation of Sardax's doomed final stand — a test never meant to be won. Emerging as themselves on the simulation deck, they moved through orientation: administration, cadet quarters, the sky dock, the quartermaster's stores, a helm exercise at the Spelljammer Nexus, and a punishing gymnasium assault course. A final errand to deliver a crate to Mirt turned into a fight when worm-like centipede creatures burst from it; Sol subdued the last one alive as evidence. The wardrobe in Mirt's chambers opened onto bounded astral night, and Casey followed a vision and a voice telling him 'Go there.'
fields.Character Beats: Sol stepped silently behind Boogie to back him in a bunk dispute and later subdued a creature rather than killing it. Boogie chose care over glory throughout, declared he wanted to keep the ship alive rather than take the helm, and shared his lonely drifting past with Tumak, promising the crew would help find Tumak's family. Casey slipped into the wardrobe, stole a shirt, and etched the constellations he saw. Gregory saw through the gym's first illusion and felt a new pull in his core. Tumak claimed a crimson bag of holding and made a hidden corner of his bunk.
fields.New Clues / Reveals: The Moonraider battle was a simulation of Sardax's final defeat. Mirt's wardrobe is a magical replica of a place beyond H’catha in the Viren star system, gifted by a spellcaster named Zerathis. A voice told Casey to 'Go there.' The attack on Mirt was likely a diversion; more burglaries struck the academy simultaneously. Boogie carries an incomplete model spelljamming ship formed inside him.
fields.NPC / Faction Movement: Boatswain Tarto oversaw the cadets' testing and orientation. Sor’Kur issued packets and access stars. Kip and Pik taught helm anatomy at the sky dock. Saerthe Abizjn ran the Nexus helm exercise. Mr. Blip outfitted the cadets and later arrived with officers confirming coordinated burglaries. Mirt rewarded the cadets and revealed the wardrobe's origin to Casey.
fields.Consequences: A live centipede creature was preserved as evidence in the crate. Casey now has a direction toward Viren. Small loyalties formed among the crew. Tumak hides stolen items behind his bunk curtains.
fields.Next Session Pressure: A living clue in a crate awaits examination, burglaries are spreading through Caelestis, a hidden path toward Viren beckons Casey, and something unfinished is taking shape inside Boogie.

fields.Major Events: Bartholomew, a newly arrived wilder cadet, was oriented by Boatswain Tarto and sent to the Weeping Goddess refectory, where the crew gathered over a meal served by Petty Officer Winston Ryeback. The cadets sorted out their shipboard roles and Bartholomew's natural affinity settled the open spelljammer's seat. Boogie, Gregory, and Bartholomew ran a second helm exercise at the Spelljammer Nexus with Saerthe, while Casey walked a Sea Dock cargo job — ending up at Rindle Gearloft's dock by mistake — and later sat at the Sky Dock, where the familiar presence returned to him. The next morning, both cadet crews ran a simulated salvage race for a logbook aboard a derelict in an asteroid field; the crew pushed through an electrical storm, recovered the logbook, fended off a githyanki vessel, and returned first.
fields.Character Beats: Bartholomew took to the helm as if born to it and, during the simulation, slowed the ship to give Boogie a way back aboard. Casey drew Ryeback's private life out of him with warmth, worked a cargo shift for pay, sat with grief for his brother at the Sky Dock, and quick-thinking duplicated the logbook. Sol took a stroke of misfortune onto himself to save Boogie's jump and heard Beshaba laugh, naming the presence at last. Boogie set the model ship on the table for the crew, insisted Gregory take the helm, then leapt onto the enemy ship and had to be brought back. Gregory plotted the course, named targets, and mused on the etiquette of stranded vessels. Tumak took the captain's chair, was quietly observed by Casey in the bathroom, and warned the table that things going missing might matter.
fields.New Clues / Reveals: Saerthe's own miniature spelljamming ship has been stolen — the same model that came out of Boogie's chest the night before, tying Boogie's unexplained object to the academy thefts. Sol identified the presence dogging his luck as Beshaba. Casey again felt the familiar presence that spoke from Mirt's wardrobe, this time at the Sky Dock. Ryeback mentioned a cadet named Barret talking about a hadozee who could read birthdays.
fields.NPC / Faction Movement: Boatswain Tarto oriented Bartholomew and took cadets to the Nexus rather than a simulation chamber. Petty Officer Winston Ryeback ran the Weeping Goddess kitchen and served the crew. Miken shared the crew's table, was gently sent off, and later silenced Tumak's snoring with a spell beyond his year. Saerthe ran the second helm exercise and briefly cracked over his stolen miniature ship. Rindle Gearloft put Casey to work at his dock and paid him. Saerthe and Tarto together briefed the salvage simulation.
fields.Consequences: Bartholomew is settled as the crew's spelljammer. The stolen-ship revelation links Boogie's mystery object to the burglaries. Sol carries a new, named awareness of Beshaba. Casey earned coin and confirmed the presence follows him beyond the wardrobe. The crew recovered the simulated logbook and won the race.
fields.Next Session Pressure: The connection between Boogie's model ship and Saerthe's stolen vessel remains unspoken, the burglaries deepen, Casey's guiding presence grows more insistent, and Sol must reckon with Beshaba's attention.

fields.Major Events: In the smoking aftermath of the salvage simulation, Gregory pried an arcane device from the wall — a rune-engraved rod built to feed on ambient magic and detonate, now spent — and it was recovered by Saerthe and Boatswain Tarto, who noted a marking on it: Vocath. That afternoon the crew split: Tumak and Gregory searched the Spelljammer Nexus terminals and Saerthe's desk, hitting a fleet-clearance lock, while Boogie and Sol traced the crate to the Sky Dock. A station-wide summons brought all six cadets to the bridge, where Mirt named Vocath as an old enemy who bore him a grudge, tasked them to check the teaching rooms and look into Joffrey and a man named Jeffrey, paid them for the simulation win and their discretion, and granted sailor-level clearance. Days later, Tarto woke them at four in the morning: an adamantine meteor had struck the spire on H’catha, and they were to crew an abandoned tyrant ship to recover it. Aboard, they found clockwork horrors feeding on a broken autognome, Ostekk-6, and Gregory opened a fight to save it — then dispatched the horrors, cleared a lantern-wisp bloom choking the access shafts, and held to rest before descending further.
fields.Character Beats: Gregory spotted, extracted, and assessed the arcane rod, searched the Nexus for answers, and later pulled the broken autognome Ostekk-6 to safety with a Vortex Warp before turning on its attackers — an act of mercy that marked him. Boogie caught the word 'Vocath' before Saerthe drew the rod back, described his childhood tribal sacrifice and the sense of being watched, and dreamed of countless other versions of himself as a converging presence pressed down on him. Sol worked a cargo manifest at the Sky Dock, learned shipments route through Mr. Blip toward Toril and H’catha, heard a curious voice in the night ask if he had truly escaped his origin, and took the front and ill luck onto himself in the shaft fight. Tumak found a glowing half-rune on his foot and another on his shoulder, mentioned Joffrey to Mirt, glimpsed 'fleet intelligence archive' on Mirt's notepad, argued successfully for expanded clearance, opened a telepathic link to Ostekk-6, cast his first fire bolt, and summoned his soul knife for the first time — feeling a tether toward home as the Rune Keeper guided the blade. Casey pulled rival cadets upright, led the way in ice armor aboard the tyrant ship, held the line beside Sol, cast Arms of Hadar through his constellations, and climbed the crew down. Bartholomew shifted into a two-starred constellation form he recalled from a childhood fall, dropped a match down the bottomless quarters shaft, and took a hard shock from a wisp.
fields.New Clues / Reveals: The arcane rod bore the marking 'Vocath,' whom Mirt named as an old enemy holding a grudge against him, making anyone connected to Mirt a target. The Sky Dock crate bore the same symbol as the rod; its contents route through Mr. Blip, with Toril and H’catha as destinations. 'Fleet intelligence archive' appeared both on a locked Nexus terminal and on Mirt's own notepad. Tumak bears two separate half-runes, each half of a different whole. Aboard the tyrant ship: a shape-shifting mimic hides among the contents, a lantern-wisp bloom has overrun much of the vessel, and something other than the flowers keeps the wisps present after the bloom is cut.
fields.NPC / Faction Movement: Saerthe and Tarto examined and secured the rod; Saerthe produced an illusion of it before Mirt. Mirt summoned the cadets, named Vocath, directed them toward Joffrey and a man named Jeffrey, rewarded and cleared them. Petty Officer Ryeback joined the tyrant-ship crew as cook, alongside deckhands Krik’Lit, a thri-kreen, and Pffred, a plasmoid. Miken kept vigil at the infirmary beside his injured crewmates Veena and Derek. The transport Flighty Foundling delivered the crew and departed. Ostekk-6, a broken autognome, warned the crew of the ship's dangers through a telepathic link.
fields.Consequences: The crew gained sailor-level clearance and a heavy coin reward. Vocath is now a named threat tied to Mirt. The crew committed to crewing an abandoned beholder tyrant ship to recover the meteor on H’catha, took two hard fights back to back with no rest, saved Ostekk-6, cleared the wisp-choked shafts, and chose to hold and recover before descending deeper.
fields.Next Session Pressure: A mimic waits somewhere aboard the tyrant ship, the wisps persist by some unknown cause, a bottomless shaft and a deck below remain unexplored, the meteor on H’catha still needs recovering, and Vocath's grudge against Mirt hangs over everything.

name: All Things Find Their Way Home

fields.Major Events: The fight in the cargo hold opened as Gregory's spell landed: three mantis-shaped clockwork horrors turned from the broken autognome they had been feeding on and set on the crew. Sol took the front and Casey held the line beside him; Gregory opened with magic missiles, then pulled the helpless autognome — Ostekk-6, named on the cargo manifest — clear of the danger with a Vortex Warp before the horrors were put down. Ostekk-6's arcane core was intact but its body was a mechanical ruin beyond magical repair, and it had no voice. Out of frustration Tumak opened a telepathic link between himself, Gregory, and Ostekk-6, and through it the autognome warned of a shape-shifting mimic among the ship's contents, a bloom overrunning the vessel, and more clockwork horrors aboard. The crew reminded themselves of the goal — route the spelljamming helm up through the ship's access shafts to the command deck and install it — using a magical floating dolly to bear the helm's weight. Testing the vertical passages, Bartholomew dropped a lit match down the bottomless quarters shaft and watched wisps rise toward the light; the garden shaft was found choked with a lantern-wisp bloom. Sol led the assault on the flowers, and a hard fight followed against wisps that proved far tougher than they looked. Tumak summoned his soul knife for the first time to end it, his runes flaring and the Rune Keeper's voice bending the wide throw true to strike the last wisp.
fields.Character Beats: Sol moved to the front and stayed there through both fights, casting Arms of Hadar and Divine Sense and Sacred Flame, and used his Misfortune's Favor to take ill luck onto himself and make the save through it. Casey held the line beside Sol and cast his own Arms of Hadar rendered through his constellations, tentacles of starlight filling the shaft. Gregory opened with magic missiles and pulled Ostekk-6 to safety with a Vortex Warp — a mercy the table felt — and understood the autognome's wound was mechanical, not magical. Tumak, frustrated by the silence, opened a telepathic link he did not know he had, cast his first fire bolt, and summoned his soul knife for the first time, feeling a tether toward home as the Rune Keeper guided the blade. Bartholomew shifted into a starry two-starred form he recognized from a childhood fall, dropped a match down the quarters shaft, and took a full shock from a wisp for ten damage. Boogie, as medic, understood alongside Gregory that Ostekk-6 could not be mended by magic.
fields.New Clues / Reveals: Through the telepathic link Ostekk-6 revealed a shape-shifting mimic hides among the ship's contents, a lantern-wisp bloom has overrun much of the vessel, and the clockwork horrors were not the only ones aboard. The autognome confirmed the way to the command deck runs through the access shafts, and that killing a flower does not unmake the wisps already loose — something else keeps them present. Bartholomew's inner starry form bears two stars, a shape he carried since a childhood fall. Tumak's soul knife is drawn through a small portal that is a piece of the home he seeks, and the tether he felt is a connection to it rather than a direction.
fields.NPC / Faction Movement: Ostekk-6, saved by the crew, guided them through the telepathic link, warning of the ship's dangers and the route to the command deck. Miken, Ryeback, and Pffred the plasmoid were present as the crew settled and took stock. The Rune Keeper spoke to Tumak as his soul-knife throw went wide, saying quietly that all things find their way home.
fields.Consequences: The crew dispatched the clockwork horrors without serious hurt, saved Ostekk-6, and cleared the lantern-wisp bloom in the garden shaft — but learned the wisps persist by some unknown cause and that they can kill. Bloodied by two hard fights with no rest between, the crew chose for the first time since boarding not to push forward, deciding to hold and recover before descending to the deck below by rope.
fields.Next Session Pressure: A mimic still hides aboard, the wisps persist by a cause the crew does not understand, a deck below waits reachable only by rope, and the helm still must be routed up the shafts to the command deck. Something is waiting below for the crew to try.

fields.Major Events: The crew chose not to rest and pressed on from the cargo hold. Boogie gave the legless Ostekk-6 a pair of legs made from a small, wrongly built piece of himself, and the crew left the helm above with Sol, Ryeback, Pffred and Krik'Lit while the rest drifted down the shaft under Boogie's slowing charm to the Hollow Deck. There they found the ship's other units torn apart among wrecked clockwork horrors, and Gregory followed a pull in his chest to Ostekk-2, the one unit still holding a light, and woke it with a jolt of lightning. The clang of Boogie's shield woke a metal creature coiled in the corner, a mechanical copy of a behir that Ostekk-2 said the original Ostekk had sent. The fight went badly: Bartholomew went down in its jaws and was brought back with Tumak's potion, and when its screech drew three clockwork horrors into the room Boogie called the retreat. Boogie missed the rope and fell down the shaft, burning a gap through the flowers below him with holy fire; the others followed and found a plane where the ship's gravity turned over, and beyond it the Command Deck. There magic failed, wisps rose from the flowers and drained whoever they latched onto, and at the room's heart lay a dead beholder overgrown by a great flower, its central eye still cancelling magic. Tumak worked out that the helm belonged on the platform beneath the body. Miken followed them down, and the crew climbed back to the cargo hold, the helm and the others.
fields.Character Beats: Boogie built Ostekk-6 a pair of legs out of himself, wrapped the crew in his own gel and a slowing charm for the descent, blessed the crew as the behir woke, launched Ostekk-6 across the room with a leaping charm, called the retreat, and after missing the rope fell through the flowers and found the gravity plane. Gregory found the remains of Ostekk-8 and Ostekk-4, followed a pull in his chest to wake Ostekk-2, opened his own chest to fire twin jets of water at the behir, and felt the pull again on the Command Deck, stronger and pointing at the beholder's body. Tumak called up his soul knives for the second time in his life, threw up a shield of force the behir's bite could not break, poured his potion into Bartholomew, and worked out where the helm must go. Casey split into copies of himself and cut into the behir from the walls, saw that it had been coiled around something giving off a soft light, and glided down through the gravity plane without the rope. Bartholomew lit the way down, fought the behir with frost and water, went down in its jaws and came back, threw back a horror with thunder, and found on the Command Deck that his magic would not answer. Sol stayed above with Ryeback and the deckhands to guard the helm.
fields.New Clues / Reveals: Ostekk-6 is a unit, an automaton, one of nine that served the ship's master, Vaelorix, a beholder who simply floated between decks; the creatures destroyed nearly all the others. Below the cargo space lie the Hollow Deck, once for repairs and maintenance with a repair bay that might mend Ostekk-6, and below that the Command Deck. The mechanical behir was sent, Ostekk-2 believed, by the original Ostekk, a brilliant tinkerer, and Ostekk-2 knew no weakness for it. Partway down the shaft is a plane where the ship's gravity turns over. On the Command Deck magic fails: the dead beholder's central eye still cancels it. Wisps bloom from the flowers there, latch on and drain whoever they touch, and become solid enough to strike once latched. Clockwork horrors stand frozen mid-stride among the flowers, and Ostekk-6 slows there but keeps going. The helm belongs on the platform where the beholder's body lies. Casey saw the behir coiled around something giving off a soft light.
fields.NPC / Faction Movement: Miken joined the descent, came down the rope after the crew, and saw the dead beholder for himself. Ostekk-2 was woken and left on the Hollow Deck. The behir and three clockwork horrors hold the Hollow Deck. Ryeback set up a camp kitchen and, with Pffred and Krik'Lit, stayed above with Sol to guard the helm.
fields.Consequences: The behir is alive and wounded on the Hollow Deck, between the cargo hold and the Command Deck. Bartholomew nearly died in its jaws and Tumak's potion is spent. A rope now runs down the shaft to the gravity plane. The crew knows where the helm must go but not how to install it where magic fails.
fields.Next Session Pressure: Get a helm of two to three hundred pounds down past the Hollow Deck and the behir, through the gravity plane, and onto the Command Deck platform, in a room where magic will not work and wisps drain whoever they touch.
